query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy caloric alloy with 0.2 at.% boron will increase its load-bearing integrity by grain-boundary strengthening while preserving its magnetocaloric and barocaloric performance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast and annealed (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibiting a martensitic transformation near 310 K with fracture toughness K_IC ≈10 MPa√m and caloric entropy changes ΔS_mag ≈15 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹ (2 T) and ΔS_bar ≈12 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹ (0.5 GPa).
generation.intervention: Add 0.2 at.% B into the melt followed by homogenization at 900 °C for 24 h and water quenching.
generation.conditions: Magnetic field up to 2 T; hydrostatic pressure up to 0.5 GPa; temperature range 280–320 K; cyclic compressive stress up to 200 MPa.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregation at prior-austenite grain boundaries and formation of nanoscale boride precipitates (10–50 nm) along boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Grain-boundary B increases cohesion and crack-deflection toughening, improving fracture resistance without substantially altering the martensitic lattice parameters or magnetic exchange interactions responsible for caloric entropy changes.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fracture toughness increases by ≈25% (to K_IC ≈12.5 MPa√m); ΔS_mag and ΔS_bar remain within ±5% of baseline.
generation.baseline: Untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy: K_IC ≈10 MPa√m, ΔS_mag ≈15 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹ (2 T), ΔS_bar ≈12 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹ (0.5 GPa).
generation.boundary: Applies for B additions ≤0.5 at.%, fields ≤2 T, pressures ≤0.5 GPa, T=280–320 K, mechanical loads ≤200 MPa.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—potential unknown effects of B on transformation hysteresis and magnetic ordering.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sample sets: (1) baseline alloy, (2) B-microalloyed (0.2 at.%). Perform fracture toughness tests and measure ΔS under 2 T magnetic field and 0.5 GPa pressure at 300 K.
measurements: ΔS_bar via direct calorimetric measurement under hydrostatic pressure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if B-microalloyed samples show <15% increase in K_IC or >5% deviation in ΔS_mag or ΔS_bar relative to baseline.
